greens.typical_stimp: About 10 for resort play (Pebble Beach); 10.5 at the 2018 AT&T Pro-Am (GCSAA); faster than 12, settling at 13-15, for U.S. Opens (Pebble Beach).
greens.notes: Smallest greens on the PGA TOUR (average 3,500 sq ft vs ~6,600 Tour average); average depth 26 paces; every green pitched back-to-front except No. 5; greens generally break toward the ocean. Five original 1919 greens remain (Nos. 6, 10, 12, 16, 18). Greens mowed to 0.125 in for the 2018 Pro-Am and 0.100 in for the 2023 U.S. Women's Open. Restorations: 9 (2013), 17 (2015), 14 (2016), 13 (2017), 11 (2021), 8 (2022), 10 (2025). Fairways/rough ryegrass and Poa annua.

boundaries.ob_summary: Confirmed OB: No. 15 right (Seventeen Mile Drive) and No. 18 right (road and white stakes). One unofficial report puts OB left of the cart path on No. 14. No official local-rules sheet or Notice to Players listing every OB line was found. For resort play, Pebble Beach's pace-of-play sheet says it uses a local rule replacing stroke-and-distance for lost or OB balls: drop at the nearest fairway edge with a two-stroke penalty (Model Local Rule E-5 style). Sources: S8, S26, S37, S38.
boundaries.penalty_area_summary: The Pacific Ocean (Stillwater Cove and Carmel Bay/Carmel Beach) and its cliffs are penalty areas, not OB. The ocean is in play from No. 4 through No. 10 (right side on 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10; around the green on 7; crossed on the approach to 8) and again on 17 (left/long) and 18 (full length left, behind a sea wall). Cliffs reach roughly 70-100 ft at No. 8, where the red line was moved 6 ft back from the edge in 2022. Inland barrancas or ravines cross No. 2 (about 100 yds short of the green), No. 3 (off the tee), No. 15 (off the tee) and No. 16 (in front of the green); their marking colour was not confirmed.

gaps: Scorecard: the official pebblebeach.com scorecard PDF (PebbleBeach-Scorecard.pdf) returned a client error and could not be read. Multi-tee yardages, handicaps and ratings come from GolfPass (S1, undated), whose Blue per-hole yardages match pebblebeach.com (S2) and OpenGolfAPI (S42). Every tee's per-hole yards sum to its published total.

Scorecard conflict: older Pebble Beach material and Greenskeeper's 2020 data list Blue as 6,828 yds with different per-hole yards and stroke indexes (e.g. No. 1 = 8, No. 18 = 3). Pebble Beach's resort brochure (S41) gives a 75.1 rating. The current listing is used here: 6,802 yds, rating 74.9, slope 144.

Ratings: no rating or slope is published for the combination tees (Gold/White, White/Green, Green/Red), or for Blue for women. No published rating was found for the U.S. Open or AT&T setups (Wikipedia's 75.9/148 'U.S. Open' rating has no official source). The U.S. Women's Open 2023 tee takes its yardage from S6 and its 79.5/152 women's rating from the USGA Target Score sheet (S7), which describes the Championship tees on the U.S. Women's Open setup. S7 also gives a men's 73.4/147 for that setup, which is not attached here.

Elevation: a published tee-to-green figure in feet was found only for No. 7 (about 40 ft downhill, from a 1917 description). The others carry only qualitative uphill or downhill notes, or nothing. No. 6 is described as climbing 'nearly four stories' and No. 14 as playing '15 yards uphill'; neither was converted to feet.

Out of bounds: hole-specific OB was confirmed only on 15 and 18; No. 14 left rests on a single player blog. OB status for the other 15 holes is unknown (null), not false, because no local-rules sheet was accessible.
Penalty areas: red or yellow marking is not confirmed for any hole except the red line on No. 8. Barranca marking on 2, 3, 15 and 16 is unconfirmed.

Green size: per-hole square footage was found only for 8 (~3,100), 14 (3,755) and 17 (5,123). The 11th's 2,200 sq ft (2019) predates its 2021 restoration, so it is left null. No sizes were found for 1-7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 16 or 18.

Green depth and width: depth in yards was found only for No. 7 (~20). Depths in paces exist for 4 (26), 8 (21-22), 9 (23), 14 (25) and 17 (left half 16) and are kept in the features text rather than converted. No green widths were found.

Green conflicts: on No. 14, GolfPass gives 3,755 sq ft while Pebble Beach says 'nearly 4,000', and the expansion is variously given as +800, +1,000 or 25%. On No. 17, sources give 5,123 or ~5,000. On No. 13, the 2017 gain is given as +400 or +300. On No. 9, the 2013 gain is given as +600 or ~700. On No. 8, the restored size is ~3,100 (2,700 + 400) or 'just over 3,000' (+300). The 8th green depth is 21 or 22 paces in two Pebble Beach articles.

Cliff height at No. 8 conflicts: ~70 ft (Golf Digest; CBS graphic 68 ft) vs ~100 ft (Pebble Beach 'Cliffs of Doom', GOLF.com instruction). The PGA TOUR says the fairway is ~10 stories above the ocean.
Bunker count: 118 (Pebble Beach, GCSAA) vs 117 (PGA TOUR).
Hole names: Pebble Beach holes have no official names; name is null for all.
Current daily green speed: only resort ~10 (undated) and a 2018 tournament figure of 10.5 were found.
The 2019 U.S. Open tee entry is par 71 because No. 2 played as a par 4; hole pars in this file are resort pars (72).
